content:
incident-bot: ALERT: gpu_pool_saturation detected in cluster acmehealth-edge-1 (private). 95% GPU utilization, pending pod queue > 420. Triggering paging.
jamie (oncall): paging in. I'm taking lead. looking at metrics now.
maya (sre): thx @jamie. I can see a big queue on the inference-queue for tenant acmehealth-prod, backlog growth started ~12:03 UTC.
samir (customer-eng): customer reports timeouts on /v1/generate and increased latency. Customer visible impact.
jamie (oncall): quick summary from grafana: GPU util ~96-98% across pool, pending pods 48, node pool target=5, max=6, current nodes=5. HPA/Autoscaler trying to add but stuck at 6 due to node boot failures.
liam (infra): looking at autoscaler logs: "maxNodeProvisionAttemptsExceeded" and repeated "imagePullBackOff" on init for the onprem-ami. Suspecting registry throttling and slow boot networking.
maya (sre): attaching recent autoscaler excerpt: ```2026-03-15T12:09:22Z autoscaler: scaleUp failed: timed out waiting for nodes to be ready; last error: timed out waiting for kubelet to register
2026-03-15T12:12:03Z cloud-provider: createNode request accepted; status=Provisioning
2026-03-15T12:14:10Z cloud-provider: node bootstrap failed: failed to fetch image: error reading manifest: rate limited
``` 
jamie (oncall): thanks. short-term mitigation ideas: 1) evict non-critical pods (dev/test) from acme cluster 2) temporarily reduce batch size to free GPU memory 3) enable fallback to hosted small-model for a subset of traffic.
samir (customer-eng): customer prefers no traffic steering if avoidable. They want us to restore capacity first.
liam (infra): I can force-provision two warm nodes from spare rack (onprem warm pool). But need approval; will take ~9-12min to boot and join.
jamie (oncall): do it. mark action: @liam force-provision warm nodes from rack-b. also evict dev namespaces: `kubectl drain node-*/dev -l tenant=dev --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` (I'll run once warm nodes are requested).
maya (sre): running eviction on low-priority pods now. Expect ~+30% immediate GPU availability once dev pods terminated.
nora-tenant-eng: heads up — dev namespaces have a long-running job that might fail; notifying owners now.
incident-bot: PAGING: @oncall -> @jamie escalation timer started (30m).
jamie (oncall): update: forced warm nodes requested. cloud console shows 2 new nodes booting. but bootstrap logs still show intermittent image pulls failing 1/10.
liam (infra): looking at rack network, we have transient DNS timeouts to the image registry (internal proxied registry). Engaging network team via #eng-infra; pinging @net-ops.
maya (sre): immediate customer impact assessment: estimated request success rate down to 22% for acmehealth-prod over last 15m. 99th latency > 6s for successful, timeouts ~12%.
samir (customer-eng): flagging priority: P1 customer reported errors; recommend elevated support and proactive messaging.
jamie (oncall): drafting message to customer: "We're seeing GPU pool saturation due to node bootstrap delays; engineers are provisioning warm nodes and evicting non-critical jobs. We'll provide ETA in 15m." Samir, want to send now?
samir (customer-eng): yes, send. include workaround: temporary routing to hosted model if lat > 2s.
liam (infra): network team (mike) responded: proxy has burst limit hit, temporarily increased rate limit for acmehealth images and cleared backlog. new nodes progressing to Docker pull ok.
maya (sre): new nodes joined cluster at 12:28 UTC. kubelet registered, kube-proxy ready. Autoscaler still marking nodes ready but pod scheduling backlog persists while image cache warms.
jamie (oncall): running `kubectl get pods -n acmehealth-prod | grep Pending` shows many init-containers stuck on pulls. I'll apply an imagePullPolicy=IfNotPresent override on non-critical pods to speed scheduling.
liam (infra): applied image cache priming on new nodes, pulling commonly used GPU images in background.
incident-bot: NOTE: follow-up task created: INC-7421 "prime onprem image cache" assigned to liam.
maya (sre): measurable improvement: pending pods down from 48 -> 12 over 7 minutes, GPU util dropping to ~72%.
samir (customer-eng): customer reports reduced error rate. still seeing intermittent 503s but improving.
jamie (oncall): handoff note: my shift ends in 20m. I'll prepare context for next oncall. If anything spikes back >90% or pending pods >20, please page me in addition to new oncall.
liam (infra): noted. I'll stay for handoff; will also keep warm nodes until autoscaler proven stable.
jamie (oncall): handing to @liam for monitoring and next steps. Handoff summary: cause = registry proxy rate-limit + slow node bootstrap, effect = GPU pool saturation and pod queue growth, mitigations applied = forced warm nodes, dev eviction, image cache priming, imagePullPolicy overrides, customer routing fallback available. ETA for normal ops = 15-25m from now.
incident-bot: HANDOFF recorded: from jamie to liam at 12:40 UTC. Pager duty updated.
liam (infra): acknowledged handoff. I'll monitor for 45m then escalate if reoccur.
maya (sre): post-incident immediate action items: 1) increase image proxy burst allowance for critical customers, 2) add a warm node buffer in acme region, 3) add autoscaler healthcheck to alert earlier if bootstrap failures observed.
samir (customer-eng): will coordinate customer comms and follow-up RCA meeting tomorrow.
jamie (oncall): final note: no data lost. impact scoped to inference latency and 5xx rate. Logged suggested postmortem tags: #onprem #gpu #autoscaler #image-registry
liam (infra): thanks all. closing incident channel after 1hr if stable. will create follow-up tickets for warm pool and registry changes.
incident-bot: INCIDENT_STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. closed-by: jamie (oncall) -> handoff to liam.
